acceptance.evidence: api.test.ts 'registers a worker session ... without touching the issue's active phase' and 'keeps the implementer as the active phase when a finished reviewer's relaunch registers ...' Rig: POST /worker/started for the finished planner (same session, no assignment) with implementer active -> 200, log '[legion] legion-sjawhar370-legsmoke-91-planner registered session 01a098c5-... while LEGSMOKE-91's active phase is implementer; the phase changes only when an architect assignment is delivered', {phases, roles} diff empty (tester-proof.md 'Acceptance 1 on the real daemon'; evidence 1-reregister-*).

acceptance.criterion: 2 the architect's most recent assignment becomes the active phase once delivered (fresh spawn at ready, or prompted into a live worker)
acceptance.evidence: Rig: planner assignment (migrated from v24) delivered at /worker/ready 03:18:04Z -> phases[LEGSMOKE-91]={planner,01a098c5}; implementer 03:23:05Z -> {implementer,01a098ca}; tester 03:26:03Z -> {tester,01a098cc} (state-d-delivered, state-1-implementer-active, state-e-after-ready). Unit: existing api/processes cases reworded to the assignment write.

acceptance.criterion: 3 spawn_worker into a live worker (resumed) sets the phase; a reconnect-only resume does not
acceptance.evidence: Rig: spawn_worker implementer against the live idle implementer -> {status:resumed}, no new pane, phases tester->implementer (state-3-*); daemon restart (c) reconnected both live shims with {phases, roles} byte-identical (state-c-*). Unit: processes.test.ts prompt path.

acceptance.criterion: 4 the newer worker's completion is accepted after an older worker relaunched
acceptance.evidence: api.test.ts 'accepts the implementer's completion after a finished reviewer relaunched' (mutation 1 fails it). Rig: after the finished planner re-registered, the live implementer's `legion handoff complete` -> '[handoff] Warning: phase recorded; no architect was live to receive the summary' (202 path, no 409); phases[LEGSMOKE-91].completed recorded (4-log.txt, state-4-after).

acceptance.criterion: 5 events route to the active phase's worker after a relaunch
acceptance.evidence: api.test.ts 'keeps the implementer as the active phase ... and keeps routing to the implementer' (routeActive -> publish to the implementer's role token; mutation 1 fails it). Not drivable on the rig in SMOKE_WEBHOOK_MODE=none (no PR in state.prs, no ingress).

acceptance.criterion: 6 daemon AGENTS.md states the active phase changes only on an architect assignment
acceptance.evidence: jj diff -r 3a9b01eb packages/daemon/src/daemon/AGENTS.md: /worker/started row ('Never writes the issue's active phase ...'), /worker/ready row ({kind: assignment|catchup}), spawn_worker invariant bullet (one writer; catch-up eligibility; sub-architect exemption; never replaces a pending assignment).

acceptance.criterion: 7 a catch-up never writes phases[issue] and is not sent to a role that is neither active nor holding a pending assignment; a sub-architect is exempt
acceptance.evidence: processes.test.ts 'skips the catch-up for a finished phase worker ...' (mutation 3), 'delivers a queued catch-up at worker/ready without touching the issue's active phase' and 'resumes a sub-architect ...' (mutation 2; the sub-architect test seeds phases[child]=planner at line 5721 and asserts the prompt at 5737 and the unchanged phase at 5740). Rig (a1) idle-live finished planner and (a2) idle-retired planner: exception -> one 'no catch-up for ...' line, no pane, {phases, roles} identical; (b) dead active implementer: --resume relaunch with pendingAssignment {kind: catchup}, same session re-registered, catch-up delivered, phases unchanged throughout (a1-*, a2-*, b-*).

acceptance.criterion: 8 a catch-up never replaces a queued architect assignment
acceptance.evidence: processes.test.ts 'leaves a booting claim's architect assignment untouched ...' and 'drops a catch-up inside the role lock ...' (mutation 4 fails the latter). Rig (e): fresh spawn_worker tester + exception 0.8 s later while booting -> '[legion] dropping catch-up for ...tester: the architect's assignment is queued and reaches the worker first', assignment intact, delivered at ready (e-*).

acceptance.criterion: 9 the architect skill states phases are strictly sequential and a different-role spawn_worker supersedes the active phase
acceptance.evidence: jj diff -r 3a9b01eb skills/legion-architect/SKILL.md: exactly the one sentence added to the spawn_worker bullet; no other skill text changed.

scenarios.d: main checkout's daemon wrote v24 state.json with bare-string pendingAssignment; this head booted on it: state.json.v24.bak byte-identical to main's file, v25 {kind: assignment, task}, delivered at ready after the boot watchdog relaunched the orphaned boot
scenarios.a1: finished planner idle-live + exception -> skipped, one log line, no pane, {phases, roles} identical
scenarios.a2: planner idle-retired by the daemon (600 s) + exception -> skipped, no pane, identical; positive control: spawn_worker planner -> --resume, phase moves to planner

observations: Live reproduction on the unfixed production daemon (cited from the architect): production state.json at 03:14 UTC had phases[LEGION-37]=implementer while the tester was the assigned phase, after the implementer's --resume relaunch re-registered.

A phase worker whose /worker/started falls into a daemon-down gap (the deliberate main->branch swap in (d)) stayed alive without registering until the boot watchdog's 3 alive-but-unconfirmed intervals retired and relaunched it; pre-existing boot behaviour, outside this issue.
loadState migrates in memory and writes only the .bak; disk state.json is rewritten on the first save after boot (for a few seconds it still read version 24). Pre-existing migration design.
Not hit on this run: the LEGION-39 negotiate_protocol timeout on a --resume relaunch; the LEGION-11 boot-time revokeSessionCapability TypeError (no dead confirmed worker at either restart).

Tester-side trap (not a code finding): with the profile's pi-legion-envoy 1.17.0 text-injected LEGION_GRANT preamble, a model that repeats the injected preamble in its own later commands shadows the fresh grant with a stale one and every `legion gh`/credential call 403s ('Unable to redeem LEGION_GRANT'); the fix is to emit commands without the preamble.

acceptance.criterion: 7 (delivery-time): a catch-up queued while its role was active and whose role has since stopped being the active phase is dropped with one log line at promotion or at ready, no relaunch or prompt; a queued architect assignment in the same position is still delivered; an architect's catch-up always is
acceptance.evidence: Unit: processes.test.ts 'drops a queued catch-up at promotion instead of prompting a live idle worker ...', '... instead of relaunching a retired worker ...' (both fail under mutation 5), 'drops a queued catch-up at worker/ready ...' (fails under mutation 6), 'delivers a sub-architect's queued catch-up at worker/ready ...' (fails under mutation 2). Rig at 143dd0d1: (g) --resume boot with {kind: catchup}, phase moved to planner during the boot -> at ready 'dropping queued catch-up for ...implementer at ready: ... active phase is planner', readyConfirmedAt set, pending cleared, no prompt in the transcript, phases unchanged; (f) cap 1, catch-up queued behind a booting tester while the implementer was active, tester's ready moved the phase, drain -> 'dropping queued catch-up for ...implementer: ... active phase is tester', queue [], pending cleared, no relaunch pane, resumeSessionFile intact, phases = tester unchanged; (f2) same with the implementer alive-idle -> enqueueIdleWorker, dropped at promotion, no prompt reached the pane; (h) control: queued assignment for the retired implementer -> promoted with --resume and delivered, phases = implementer.

rounds.regression: handleWorkerStarted (no phase write; bystander log gains role !== 'architect'), promptExistingWorker (assignment-only write), resumeWorker pre-checks, the deliverToWorker lock-side guard, and the v24->v25 migration are code-identical to 910c527f apart from comments and log labels (activePhaseLabel: a completed phase now logs 'none'); mutations 1-4 fail the same tests as in round 1; round-1 rig evidence for Acceptance 1-9 stands, and the round-2 rig re-exercised Acceptance 1 (/worker/started bystander line for the relaunched implementer), 2, 3 and 7's never-writes half along the way.
